A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MVPA/MVPFormer and SWEC dataset work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support comparison, including matching retained material across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original iEEG prediction, seizure detection, forecasting, classification, and ablation results in Section 5 and Appendices F–G.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds Brain TreeBank decoding, channel-count evaluations, and runtime/memory measurements.

M1.justification: Section 3.2 extends the downstream readout to concatenate channel embeddings for non-seizure tasks, alongside the retained channel-averaged seizure readout. The MVPA/FlashMVPA computations, encoder/decoder, contrastive pre-training, and LoRA settings remain unchanged.

E1.justification: v2 evaluates Brain TreeBank on pitch, volume, sentence-onset, and speech decoding, substantially extending iEEG task coverage beyond seizure detection and signal prediction. Brain TreeBank was only cited in v1. The original seizure datasets and general time-series benchmarks remain.

E2.justification: Brain TreeBank comparisons introduce Brant and PopT variants, including BrainBERT/TOTEM-based and location-free variants (Table S10). TimesFM is added to forecasting and classification comparisons; WPMixer is evaluated for forecasting only. Appendix A.4 also adds a measured comparison of naïve PyTorch MVPA against FlashMVPA. Existing seizure comparators remain.

E3.justification: New protocols include subject-specific fine-tuning and held-out testing on Brain TreeBank, channel-count sweeps during fine-tuning/testing, and isolated attention forward-pass benchmarks with batch size 64, embedding size 768, and time/channel dimensions from 1 to 50. Existing seizure and forecasting settings remain; replacing 99% overlap with a five-second stride is equivalent.

E4.justification: v2 adds systematic runtime/memory scaling analysis for naïve MVPA versus FlashMVPA (Tables S3–S4) and a 10–50-channel sensitivity study across four decoding tasks (Table S23). These add direct efficiency and robustness evidence. Existing pre-training, model-size, channel-selection, patient-difficulty, and connectivity analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Tables S10 and S23 introduce parenthetical variability values alongside decoding scores, although the statistic and underlying run counts are not defined. This does not establish additional repeated training runs. The existing Kappa estimation using 300 segments per subject and 250 iterations is unchanged.

E6.justification: Existing tabulated results are retained, including SWEC Kappa scores of 0.57 and 0.54. New results include MVPFormer-S Brain TreeBank accuracies of 0.83/0.88/0.87/0.90 for pitch/volume/onset/speech, additional baseline scores, and channel/runtime/memory sweeps. FlashMVPA uses 4.20 GB at T=C=50 where naïve MVPA runs out of memory. New tables disagree on MV-Llama pitch accuracy: 0.63 in Table 1 versus 0.62 in Table S10.

T1.justification: The attention and loss equations, relative-shifting derivations, structured-dropout formula, and MVPA complexity expressions are retained. The new alternative-attention discussion adds conceptual comparisons rather than new formal definitions, proofs, or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion broaden the performance claims to several iEEG tasks and explicitly claim state-of-the-art results on all four Brain TreeBank tasks. This extends the claimed downstream scope beyond v1. The claim is overstated relative to Table 1, where location-aware PopT leads on onset and speech. The three central method/model/dataset contributions remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretation of implicit channel mapping versus explicit electrode locations, acknowledging that locations benefit some decoding tasks. It also interprets the new channel-count sweep and explicitly limits model/dataset use to research, excluding diagnosis. Existing scaling limitations and seizure-related interpretations remain.

D1.justification: The SWEC access pointer changes from Medical Blocks to Hugging Face. v2 adds consent information, research-only usage conditions, and settings for the new computational benchmark. Existing architecture hyperparameters, pre-training hardware/budget, optimizer details, and project code link are retained.

R1.justification: New Appendix A.2 and Table S1 substantially expand positioning against Transformer-XL, DeBERTa, axial, criss-cross, and sparse attention, including explicit acknowledgment of antecedents to disentangled attention. New references also support wavelet encoding and comparisons with PopT, TimesFM, and WPMixer.

P1.justification: v2 revises the abstract, introduction, and conclusion, organizes Section 5.2 into seizure and Brain TreeBank subsections, and adds appendix subsections and acknowledgments. Most existing technical and analytical prose remains closely matched; the revision is primarily scientific expansion rather than extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: v2 changes document typography and reflows the layout, enlarges/redraws Figure 3, restructures Table 1, and expands the forecasting/classification tables. New appendix displays cover attention comparisons, computational costs, decoding, and channel sensitivity. The original seizure summary is relocated to Table S9, while the other existing figures are retained.

improvement.justification: The new decoding, channel-count, and computational experiments strengthen evidence for versatility and efficiency beyond v1, while expanded prior-work discussion clarifies positioning. The net gain is limited by sparse new protocol details, undefined variability statistics, inconsistent table entries, and abstract/conclusion claims of SOTA on all four decoding tasks despite PopT leading on onset and speech.
